model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity (engine route): NI to ordinary equity less CET1 retention, net debt zero

inputs.share_count_basis: ADS-equivalent millions (1 ADS = 4 ordinary 10p shares, LYG_20F_FY2016.txt:12651), so per-share values are per ADS and match the NYSE quote. Basic shares: 58,101M ranking for the 2026 interim dividend (record date 7 Aug 2026), derived as £918M / 1.58p (LYG_6K_H1-2026.txt dividend section). Share capital of £5,827M at 10p nominal gives 58,270M at 30 Jun 2026, which corroborates it. Dilutive awards add 730M (H1-26 diluted weighted average 59,234M less basic 58,504M, LYG_6K_H1-2026.txt:8178-8180). Total 58,831M ordinary = 14,707.8M ADS. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flow and buybacks are value-neutral at IV. The rest of the 2025 £1.75bn programme (about £0.55bn after 30 June) and the new £1.0bn programme (to Jan 2027) are not deducted from shares. The CET1 surplus that funds them is credited in equity_bridge instead.
inputs.sbc_source: Group 'value of employee services' (KPI StockBasedComp): FY2025 211, H1-25 102, H1-26 115, so TTM to Jun-26 = 211 - 102 + 115 = 224. SBC nets out of the bank flow because 'ebitda' adds it back and sbc_pct removes it; it only moves the street basis. reported_fcf = TTM attributable ordinary profit 4,758 + SBC 224.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 repurchases £1.71bn plus ordinary dividends £2.0bn. H1-26: £1.18bn of buybacks and £1.42bn of dividends paid. Interim dividend 1.58p (+30%), and a further buyback of up to £1.0bn to complete by 27 Jan 2027. Diluted weighted shares fell from 71,256M (FY2020) to 59,234M (H1-26).
inputs.fx_note: Flows and balance sheet are in GBP millions. The quote is USD per ADS (1 ADS = 4 ordinary shares; shares_outstanding is already in ADS-equivalents). Model-to-quote rate is 1.324 USD per GBP (Yahoo GBPUSD=X, regularMarketTime 2026-10-02T21:29Z). Parity check against the primary line: LLOY.L closed at 104.0p (2026-10-02T15:37Z) x 4 / 100 x 1.324 = US$5.51 per ADS-equivalent, within 0.2% of the NYSE ADS close at inputs.price_as_of, which confirms the rate, its direction and the 4:1 ratio. GBP flows are discounted at a GBP cost of equity and converted at spot. refresh_price.py moves the ADS price but not this rate.
inputs.wacc_rationale: GBP cost of equity of 10.0%. The 10-year gilt is about 4.6%, plus a beta of about 1.1 x 5.0% ERP = 10.1%, rounded to 10.0%. That is below BCS (11.0%, about 48% investment bank) and HSBC (10.5%, Asia/EM exposure). Lloyds is a domestic UK retail and commercial bank with a mortgage-heavy book, a structural hedge, and no material trading book. The rate is in the currency of the flows. One rate across all three scenarios: risk is carried in the bear path and its weight, not in a per-scenario premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable. The bank FCFE flow is after all operating costs, including occupancy and operating-lease depreciation (Lloyds' statutory total income is gross of the Lex/Tusker operating-lease depreciation charged in operating expenses). No separate lease adjustment.
inputs.nci_treatment: Inside the flow. AT1 coupons (£447M TTM: H2-25 218 + H1-26 229) are tax-deductible, with the relief booked in tax ('Tax relief on coupons on other equity instruments', LYG_6K_H1-2026.txt:6929), so they come out GROSS pre-tax. NCI (£131M TTM) is grossed up at about 28% to £182M. 'ebitda' = PBT + SBC - AT1 - NCI/(1-t), so the flow is profit attributable to ordinary shareholders. AT1 par (£5.55bn) is therefore NOT also deducted in the bridge (BCS/USB/WFC convention).
inputs.notes: MODEL: FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine, with net_debt = 0. SKILL.md routes banks to residual income on tangible book. The house precedent for large banks (BCS, HSBC, NAB.AX, USB, WFC) is FCFE-at-CoE on the engine route. That is the same economics (value = TNAV + PV of returns above CoE) expressed as distributable cash, and it keeps LYG comparable to BCS and HSBC. Deposits (£500.9bn) are operating funding, not debt. Debt securities (£90.9bn) and subordinated liabilities (£9.2bn) are wholesale funding and MREL, not enterprise debt. OCF is meaningless for a bank (the CSV swings from -11.1bn to +28.2bn). ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = statutory 'Total income' (net of insurance finance expense, IFRS 17 basis). TTM H2-25 + H1-26 = 10,036 + 10,626 = 20,662 (LYG_6K_H1-2026.txt income statement). 'ebitda' = PBT 7,450 + SBC 224 - AT1 447 - NCI 182 = 7,045 (34.1%). Excluding the £800M motor-finance charge in H2-25 opex, it is 7,845 (38.0%). sbc_pct removes SBC, and D&A is 0 (inside operating costs). Cash tax: UK 25% corporation tax plus the 3% bank surcharge; TTM 2,114 / (7,450 - 447) = 30.2%, inflated by the motor provision; H1-26 1,170 / 4,064 = 28.8%. 'capex' = CET1 retention that holds CET1 at the c.13.0% Board target (which includes a ~1% management buffer). Target CET1 = 13.0% x 241.8bn = 31.4bn, so CET1/revenue = 1.521 and capex% = 152.1 x g/(1+g). FY0 check: (7,045 - 224) x (1 - 30.2%) = 4,761, vs reported TTM attributable profit of 4,758. The motor-finance charge is treated as non-recurring: the year-1 margin is set from H1-26 and FY26 guidance, not from TTM. The residual risk (provision £1.95bn total; FCA scheme challenged at the Upper Tribunal, hearing not before Dec 2026) sits in the bear path.

equity_bridge.item: CET1 surplus above the c.13.0% target at 30 Jun 2026
equity_bridge.note: CET1 13.6% vs the Board's c.13.0% target: 0.6% x £241.8bn RWA = £1.45bn. The 13.6% already deducts the full £1.75bn 2025 buyback. The £1.0bn H2-26 buyback announced with the interim results is funded from this surplus, and its shares are not deducted from the share count, so the full surplus is credited. FY2025 20-F guidance: 'pay down to a CET1 ratio of c.13.0% by end of 2026'.

Not quantified in the filings (20-F FY2025 regulatory timeline lists Basel 3.1 implementation in Q1 2027). Lloyds' mortgage RWA floors were largely front-loaded in the 1 Jan 2022 changes (-230bp at the time), so the step-up is assumed modest: about £4bn RWA x 13% = c.£0.5bn of one-off retention.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr (total income FY2020-FY2025). The 3-year figure (2.2%) is depressed by the FY2024 dip, when deposit-margin compression offset the structural-hedge reinvestment. TTM income to Jun-26 is +13% y/y on H1, and FY26 guidance (underlying NII c.£14.9bn, about +7%) implies 5-6% near-term growth.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (0.3% 3yr, -0.6% 5yr) diverges by more than 30% from the revenue CAGRs (2.2% / 5.1%) and the 5-year EPS CAGR (41.9%). Lloyds distributes almost all capital generation: about £7.3bn of buybacks FY2022-H1-26 cut diluted shares by about 17%, and AT1 was redeemed. Total equity is therefore flat by design. The 5-year EPS and attributable-profit CAGRs start at the FY2020 COVID-impairment trough (EPS 1.2p) and are meaningless. The 3-year attributable-profit CAGR (-5.8%) is distorted by the FY2025 £800M motor-finance charge. Normalised FY2025 (statutory PAT ex-motor £5,428M, about £4,870M to ordinary shareholders) gives -1.0%.
historical_growth.notes: 'FCF' here is the bank owner-flow proxy: profit attributable to ordinary shareholders (SBC is already a P&L expense). Reported FCF/OCF is not meaningful for a bank. No SBC-adjusted divergence exists, because SBC is about 1% of income.

base.growth_rationale: Year 1 (Jul-26 to Jun-27) is +6%. H1-26 statutory income was +13% y/y and NII +10% as the structural hedge reprices; FY26 guidance is underlying NII c.£14.9bn. Hedge reinvestment tailwinds persist into 2027-28, then growth fades to 2.5% GBP nominal by year 8.
base.margin_rationale: H1-26 'ebitda' margin (PBT + SBC - AT1 - NCI) was 38.6%, with impairment at an elevated 616M (macro overlay). Year 1 at 38% is consistent with FY26 guidance: cost:income <50%, AQR c.25bps, RoTE >16%. It implies attributable profit of about £5.8bn and RoTE of about 17% on £33bn TNAV. Margins hold for two years as hedge income compounds, then fade to 35% (PBT margin about 37.5%) as impairment normalises to about 30bps through the cycle and deposit competition erodes the hedge spread. Terminal RoTE is about 15%, a 5pt spread over the 10% CoE.
base.capex_rationale: CET1 retention = 1.521 x g/(1+g), which holds CET1 at the 13.0% target as RWA grows with income.
base.tax_rationale: UK 25% plus 3% bank surcharge. H1-26 ETR on PBT after AT1 coupons was 28.8%; the TTM 30.2% is inflated by the partly non-deductible motor provision. Held at 28.5%.

bull.margin_rationale: The structural hedge locks in higher yields for longer, the c.£2bn of strategic-initiative revenues (wealth via Schroders Personal Wealth, Lex/Tusker, Commercial capital-lite) lands, and cost:income moves into the mid-40s. Motor-finance redress settles within the existing £1.95bn provision. Terminal RoTE is about 18-19%.

bear.margin_rationale: The BoE cuts faster into a UK slowdown, compressing deposit margins, and unemployment rises; the H1-26 macro overlay already shows a higher unemployment peak and softer house prices. Impairment reaches about 60bps in year 2 (about £2bn above base). The FCA motor-finance scheme survives the Upper Tribunal challenge with costs above the £1.95bn provision (about £1bn extra in year 2). A bank-tax increase is a further risk. Margin troughs at 28% and recovers to 33.5%. Terminal RoTE is about 12-13%, a thin spread over CoE. Retention is held at 0 in years 2-3 rather than negative.

scenario_narratives.base: Lloyds delivers its 2026 guidance (RoTE >16%, cost:income <50%, >200bps capital generation) and holds RoTE in the mid-teens. The structural hedge keeps compounding NII through 2028 while impairment normalises from very low levels. CET1 is paid down to c.13% and distributions run at about 90%+ of earnings via a progressive dividend plus half-yearly buybacks. Income growth fades to UK nominal GDP after the hedge tailwind is spent. Motor finance costs nothing beyond the existing provision.
scenario_narratives.bull: A higher-for-longer UK rate curve and the hedge roll lift NII beyond guidance. Capital-lite growth in wealth, insurance and Lex/Tusker adds about £2bn of income, and digital cost-out drives cost:income into the mid-40s. RoTE settles at 18%+, and the shares re-rate further on a pure UK-retail bank with distributions running at about 8-9% of market cap.
scenario_narratives.bear: A UK downturn arrives with faster rate cuts. Mortgage and unsecured credit losses rise to about 60bps, deposit margins compress, and the FCA motor redress scheme is upheld at a cost above the provision. Income falls 3% in year 2, buybacks pause for two years to rebuild CET1, and RoTE settles around 12-13%. That is barely above the cost of equity, which at about 1.85x TNAV leaves a long way to fall.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 20%, and bull cut from 35% to 30%. Lloyds is a pure UK-domestic lender, so its whole book is exposed to one economy and one rate cycle. The motor-finance redress outcome is unresolved (Upper Tribunal hearing not before Dec 2026), and the shares already price in strong delivery (about 1.85x TNAV, versus about 1.06x for BCS). The bear is still lighter than BCS/HSBC's 25%: Lloyds has no investment-bank or EM exposure, a mortgage-heavy book, and guidance has been raised rather than cut.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A bank is worth what it can pay ordinary shareholders after funding the capital its growth requires. The flow is profit attributable to ordinary shareholders (after AT1 coupons and NCI) less the CET1 retention that holds the ratio at the c.13% target, discounted at a GBP cost of equity of 10%. Deposits are funding, not debt, so nothing is deducted for net debt. Value is therefore TNAV plus the PV of returns above the cost of equity. At a through-cycle RoTE of about 15%, Lloyds earns a 5pt spread, which justifies roughly 1.6-1.8x TNAV. The ADS trades at about 1.85x TNAV (104p vs 56.2p), which already prices in RoTE of about 16%+ being sustained. The GBP value converts to USD per ADS at spot, so a USD holder also carries GBP translation risk.
key_risks_to_valuation: Motor-finance commission redress: the £1.95bn cumulative provision is management's best estimate. The FCA scheme (PS26/3) is under four Upper Tribunal challenges, with a hearing not before Dec 2026, and Lloyds (Black Horse) is the largest UK motor lender. Overruns sit in the bear path.
UK rate cycle: the structural hedge smooths but does not remove NII sensitivity. Faster BoE cuts plus deposit competition compress margins.
Credit: the base assumes impairment normalising to about 30bps. A UK recession at about 60bps for a year costs about £2bn pre-tax.
Valuation already rich at about 1.85x TNAV: most of the value is the spread over CoE, so a 2pt lower terminal RoTE removes about 15-20% of IV.
Basel 3.1 (from 1 Jan 2027): not quantified in the filings. A modest £0.5bn deduction is taken in the bridge.
UK bank tax and surcharge policy risk, and GBP/USD translation for ADS holders (the USD value per ADS moves one-for-one with GBPUSD).

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 4.42-6.34 (USD per ADS). FX from Yahoo GBPUSD=X; LLOY.L for the parity check.

H1-2026 Half-Year Results 6-K (LYG_6K_H1-2026.txt): three-half income statement (H1-26, H1-25, H2-25), balance sheet, CET1 13.6% / RWA £241.8bn, CET1 target c.13.0%, ordinary shareholders' equity £41,461M, goodwill and intangibles £8,732M, weighted diluted 59,234M, interim dividend 1.58p = £918M, £1.0bn further buyback, motor-finance status. FY2025 20-F (LYG_20F_FY2025.txt:20803-20830, 21564-21625): 2026 guidance and the £800M motor charge.
